In [[mathematics]], the '''Koszul cohomology''' groups <math>K_{p,q}(X,L)</math> are [[group (mathematics)|group]]s associated to a [[projective variety]] ''X'' with a [[line bundle]] ''L''. They were introduced by {{harvs|txt|last=Green|first=Mark|authorlink=Mark Lee Green|year=1984|year2=1984b}}, and named after [[Jean-Louis Koszul]] as they are closely related to the [[Koszul complex]].

{{harvtxt|Green|1989}} surveys early work on Koszul cohomology, {{harvtxt|Eisenbud|2005}} gives an introduction to Koszul cohomology, and {{harvtxt|Aprodu|Nagel|2010}} gives a more advanced survey.

==Definitions==

If ''M'' is a [[graded module]] over the [[symmetric algebra]] of a [[vector space]] ''V'', then the Koszul cohomology <math>K_{p,q}(M,V)</math> of ''M'' is the [[cohomology]] of the sequence 
:<math>\bigwedge^{p+1}M_{q-1}\rightarrow \bigwedge^{p}M_{q} \rightarrow \bigwedge^{p-1}M_{q+1}</math>
If ''L'' is a line bundle over a projective variety ''X'', then the Koszul cohomology <math>K_{p,q}(X,L)</math> is given by the Koszul cohomology <math>K_{p,q}(M,V)</math> of the graded module <math>M= \bigoplus_q H^0(L^q)</math>, viewed as a module over the symmetric algebra of the vector space <math>V=H^0(L)</math>.
